correctness.rationale: For every smooth positive periodic source with first two Fourier modes nonzero, a shared positive response length, two positive gains and arbitrary offsets/registration, the Fourier ODE yields the exact complex ratio; the invariant phase is strictly decreasing with exact range (-pi,0), giving a bijection and a monotone cubic recovery. Necessity, two-ratio sufficiency via a positive constructed field, one-harmonic nonidentifiability, and both endpoint expansions are proved. Numeric tests and exact rational witness supplement the complete argument without certifying experiments.

value.rationale: Dynamic environmental monitors can have severe spatial lag, GPS misregistration and unknown gain; unknown raw pollutant profiles rule out direct calibration. The theorem identifies an exact field-free, registration- and gain-invariant calibration statistic, classifies all admissible two-harmonic data, proves sharp data minimality, and quantifies ill-conditioning. These are a mathematically complete natural inverse measurement problem, not a renamed time-constant identity; no claim of field implementation or downstream prediction is needed.
